questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish pulse from tempo in a handover note
questions.stem: At handover, Nurse A writes that pulse and tempo are the same thing; is she correct?

options.text: No, pulse is the steady beat while tempo is the speed of that beat
Yes, because both describe how fast the music moves overall
No, pulse is the melody and tempo is the harmony
options.misconception: mixes up pulse with melodic line

options.text: Yes, because tempo changes never affect the pulse
options.misconception: assumes tempo cannot alter the felt pulse

questions.explanation: Pulse is the underlying steady beat; tempo sets how fast that beat occurs. The tempting idea that they are identical fails because tempo can change while the pulse concept remains.
questions.hint: Pulse is the beat, tempo is its speed.

questions.topic: The beat and the measure in simple meter
questions.learningObjective: Count beats in a simple-meter measure
questions.stem: During handover, a chart lists 4 beats per measure in 4/4; how many beats fill one measure?

options.text: Two beats fill the measure in 4/4 simple meter
Three beats fill the measure in 4/4 simple meter
Four beats fill the measure in 4/4 simple meter
Six beats fill the measure in 4/4 simple meter

questions.explanation: In 4/4 simple meter each measure contains four quarter-note beats. The distractors miscount by grouping or confusing meters.
questions.hint: The top number gives beats per measure.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: The beat unit in compound metre
questions.stem: In handover notes, a 6/8 passage is discussed; how many eighth notes make one dotted-quarter beat?
questions.explanation: In compound 6/8 the beat unit is the dotted quarter, which equals three eighth notes. Counting two would be a simple-meter mistake.
questions.hint: Compound meter groups three eighths per beat.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: The total duration of a measure
questions.learningObjective: Compute total measure duration in quarters
questions.stem: At handover, explain how to find the total duration of a 3/4 measure in quarter notes.

answer.exemplar: A 3/4 measure contains three quarter-note beats, so its total duration is three quarter notes, found by reading the top number as beats and the bottom as the beat unit.

questions.explanation: The top number states beats per measure and the bottom states the beat unit. Multiplying gives total duration; confusing the two numbers is the common error.
questions.hint: Top number counts beats, bottom names the unit.

questions.stem: Nurse B asks how long a dotted quarter lasts; which choice is right?

options.text: Three quarter notes, adding a whole quarter
options.misconception: adds a full quarter instead of half

options.text: Two full quarter notes, the dot doubling the value
One quarter note only, ignoring the dot entirely
One and a half quarter notes, the dot adding half a quarter

questions.explanation: A dot adds half the note's value, so a dotted quarter is one and a half quarters. Doubling or ignoring the dot are typical slips.
questions.hint: Dot equals half the note value.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.stem: In a handover chart, two notes are joined by a curved line; is it a tie or a slur?

options.text: It is a slur because curved lines always mean phrasing
It is a tie because the notes are the same pitch
It is a tie even if the pitches differ
It is a slur only when notes share the same pitch

questions.explanation: A tie joins identical pitches into one duration; a slur connects different pitches legato. The curve alone does not decide.
questions.hint: Same pitch means tie; different means slur.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.stem: At handover, describe what syncopation does to the expected accent.

answer.exemplar: Syncopation displaces the accent onto a weak beat or off-beat, so the listener's expected strong-beat accent is contradicted by the actual rhythmic stress.

questions.explanation: Syncopation shifts stress away from strong beats. The wrong view keeps accents on strong beats, which is ordinary meter not syncopation.
questions.hint: Accent moves to a weak or off beat.

Three quarter notes fit in the space of three quarters
Three quarter notes fit in the space of two quarters
Three quarter notes fit in the space of four quarters

questions.explanation: A quarter-note triplet squeezes three quarters into two quarters' time. Removing compression or inverting the ratio are common errors.

questions.topic: The beat unit in compound metre
questions.stem: During handover, a 9/8 measure is sized; how many quarter notes does it equal?
questions.explanation: Nine eighth notes equal four and a half quarter notes. Rounding down to four would be wrong.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: The total duration of a measure
questions.stem: At handover, state how to compute a measure's total duration.

answer.exemplar: Multiply the number of beats per measure by the value of the beat unit to get the total duration of one measure.

questions.explanation: Beat count times beat unit value gives total duration. Adding instead of multiplying is wrong.
